status_summary: Executive Order 14182 (signed 2025-01-24) states a policy of ending the use of federal taxpayer dollars to fund or promote elective abortion, revokes EO 14076 and EO 14079, and directs OMB to issue implementing guidance; it does not name DOD. Military.com reported in late January 2025 that the Defense Travel Management Office had updated travel regulations, citing the order, so that travel for abortion and fertility care is no longer reimbursable, and the Center for Reproductive Rights reported that DOD rescinded the travel policy on 2025-01-30. The Center also reported on 2025-02-03 that DOD rescinded a policy allowing up to 21 days of administrative absence for non-covered reproductive care. The DOD memoranda themselves were not retrieved, and the sources show no statute or rule making the change permanent.

timeline.event: EO 14182 signed, stating a policy of ending federal taxpayer funding of elective abortion, revoking EO 14076 and EO 14079 and directing OMB guidance.
DOD rescinds its travel reimbursement policy for reproductive health care, which had covered abortion travel.
Military.com reports the Defense Travel Management Office updated travel regulations, citing the executive order, so travel for abortion and fertility care is no longer reimbursable.
Center for Reproductive Rights reports DOD also rescinded the administrative absence policy for non-covered reproductive care, so service members must take leave.

At a House Appropriations hearing on the FY2026 defense appropriations bill, an amendment to reinstate the 2022 Defense Department policy on travel reimbursement and leave for abortion was voted down.

title: End DOD funding of travel and leave for service member abortions
uncertainties: The DOD memoranda were not retrieved; facts come from an advocacy organization and a news outlet (the advocacy source is cited only for the dates and content of the DOD rescissions, which the news report corroborates for the travel policy only). The Military.com article carries no date in its text; the date is from its URL. The exact date of the administrative absence rescission is not given. The sources differ on fertility care: the news report says fertility travel is no longer reimbursable, while the Center says the rescissions do not apply to assisted reproduction such as IVF. A Department of the Air Force memorandum of March 2025 on non-covered reproductive care was found in a review search on an Air Force medicine site but could not be opened. Whether military health coverage of abortion under existing law changed was not examined.
